title: Commit Message
summary: Writes a Conventional Commits message from your staged changes, shows it to you and commits only after you say yes.
description: Good commit messages explain why a change exists, and that is the part people skip when they are tired. This command reads what is staged, works out the one thing the change does and drafts a message in the Conventional Commits format.
It never stages files for you and never commits without an answer. If the staged diff mixes unrelated work, it says so and suggests how to split it.
useWhen: Right after you stage a change and want a clear message
When a diff touches several files and you are unsure of the type
On a team that uses Conventional Commits for changelogs
When you want a body that explains why, not what
body:
Write a commit message for the staged changes. Extra context from the user: $ARGUMENTS

1. Run `git diff --staged --stat` and then `git diff --staged`. If nothing is staged, stop and say so. Do not stage anything yourself.
2. Run `git log -n 10 --oneline` and copy the project's habits for scope names and tense.
3. Pick one type: feat, fix, refactor, perf, docs, test, build, ci, chore. If two types fit, the diff is probably two commits: say so and propose the split by file.
4. Write the subject as `type(scope): summary`, imperative mood, lower case, no period, at most 72 characters. Use the scope or ticket id from the user's text when given.
5. Add a body only when the reason is not obvious from the subject. Explain why the change was needed and any trade-off, wrapped at 72 columns. Add `BREAKING CHANGE:` in the footer if a public interface changed.

Show the message in a code block, then ask: "Commit with this message?" Run `git commit` only after a clear yes. Never use --no-verify and never amend an existing commit.

example.result:
fix(checkout): reject expired coupons before totals are computed

Expired coupons were applied and then removed on the confirm step, so the
cart total jumped. Validate the expiry date in applyCoupon() instead.

Refs: PAY-214

Commit with this message?

faq.question: Will it stage my files?
faq.answer: No. It only reads what you have already staged and stops if the index is empty.

faq.question: What if my changes are unrelated?
faq.answer: It tells you the diff covers two concerns and lists which files belong to each, so you can split the commit.

access: Reads the staged diff and recent commit subjects
Runs git commit only after you confirm
